log.what: Slot grammar approved and committed (59 slots, BABEL-032..090). Pilot batch queued: HIGH (COMMON ADJ), FOREIGN (UNCOMMON ADJ), ELDER (COMMON TITLE), SEED (UNCOMMON NOUN), DEEP (RARE ADJ).
Pilot running through the production pipeline: plan --auto (ability budgets + critic) -> validate -> imagegen (golden-matrix reference pack) -> visual-gate -> grade.

#034 SEED complete: 100/100. Validator calibration (5 fixes) + operator-driven text mode landed on main. Schema drifts fixed en route: game_name Towerfall->Hypertext, rarity shapes ->diamond, growth-tolerant census tests.

#032 HIGH complete at 100/100. Pipeline hardened en route: pip-row registration with bounds ('ark' proof reclassified as false rejection), 3-vote style majority, bullet-marker counting. Known open item: content score wobbles 90-100 - candidate for voting too.
#033 ELDER complete: first-attempt 100/100 - the hardening from HIGH's fight (registration, voting, marker counting) paid off immediately.

Active voice adopted set-wide (prefix boilerplate retired); all three pilot cards revoiced and re-rendered to 100/100. Self-healing loop added: render -> pip gate -> voted grade -> single-defect fix-mode revise. Descriptor gains flat-pip and verbatim-digit rules; revise.txt preview revert loophole closed.
#035 DEEP complete at 100/100 (a5). RARE tier proven: two-branch COMPLEXITY stat-check renders legibly.

Draw-one baseline power floor adopted: every ability must beat a plain 'Draw one card from the Tower.', commons only modestly. Enforced at three layers - budget table (payoff 1 = real material; COMMON widened to 3-5 with setup 0/interaction 0/payoff exactly 1 as brakes), deterministic material-action check, and a new power_floor critic category. HIGH (look-only) and ELDER (blind cycling) fell below the floor and were replanned through the full pipeline with their v1 scholarship preserved.

ROOT CAUSE of render roulette found: the 20 golden templates are blank forms containing literal placeholder text ([ABILITY DESCRIPTION HERE], CARD TITLE, DEFINITION TEXT, #XXX, '- Set' footer). Models transcribed the form instead of filling it. Worse, the style judge could not catch leaks because the reference IS the form - a leaking card looks MORE like the template. Fixes: descriptor placeholder-substitution rule, reference-free focused leak query as a hard grade gate, focused bullet recount to stop wrapped-trivia false zeros. ELDER then passed first-attempt; HIGH/SEED/DEEP faces re-rendered leak-clean.
#036 FOREIGN re-added and planned under the complete new contract (baseline floor + leak gate active from its first render).

PILOT COMPLETE: all 5 cards (HIGH, ELDER, SEED, DEEP, FOREIGN) at 100/100 with leak-clean faces and draw-one-baseline abilities. Trivia recount now guards the content scoring path too. Pipeline verdict: green for the remaining 54 slots and the 31 legacy face regenerations.

Branching style ruling: a binary condition is stated once and the remainder resolved with 'otherwise' - don't restate the complement. Encoded in the ability primer ('or else'/bare 'if not' stay banned); DEEP replanned and re-rendered under it at 100/100.

CARD-ADVANTAGE LADDER ruling: activation costs are part of the math - RARE must account for at least two cards' worth of advantage, GLORIOUS at least three; exclusive branches never stack. Encoded in the budget scale, primer, power_floor critic, and a branch-aware payoff estimator (the old DEEP is now deterministically rejected). DEEP redesigned as Sheol recovery plus draw - 'out of the deep' made literal - and re-rendered at first-attempt 100/100 with Psalm 130:1.

Design-space ruling: the generation prompt, not any one card, was the problem - it stated budgets as constraints without opening creative space, so designs reached the floor by bolting a generic draw onto a small effect. build_candidate_prompt now carries a RARITY DESIGN SPACE palette per tier plus the anti-pattern by name; hand size noted as not-pure-advantage (players empty hands into Lots), making multi-card adds a legitimate RARE stretch. DEEP finalized as a single motion: up to three deep recoveries from Sheol.

BATCH 2 COMPLETE (#037-#041): GATHER, SODOM, KINGDOM, SHINAR, MESSENGER - all 100/100, three on first attempt. First GLORIOUS proven (table-wide Sheol gathering; two-card-back cost glyph gate-verified). Cost indicator gate revived from the pre-baseline WIP and wired fail-closed into every render path after DEEP's cross-marked card back slipped past the style judge; ledger cards are now tappable with a zoom lightbox.

VERSE LEXICAL RULE (user): the printed OT verse must contain the card's Hebrew lemma and the NT verse its Greek lemma, and every ref-strip entry likewise - allusion-only verses (Luke 17:32 for SODOM) are out. Audit found 9 of 10 cards in violation; all patched at content level and re-rendered panel-only (image-only revises keep approved art). SHINAR's Greek panel now carries the NT's own name for the land (Babylon, Rev 18:2). Rule encoded in the metadata prompt, docs/prompt-recipe.md, and memory. Also: cost-indicator gate revived and made fail-closed on every render path; extra 'ORIGINAL LANGUAGES' heading now rejected by the leak gate; image-only revises write a prompt sidecar instead of mutating prompt.txt.

BATCH 3 COMPLETE (#042-#046): TONGUE, CHOOSE, DARK, FILLED, WATCHMAN. First batch on the gemini-3.7-flash judge and the first run of the spool daemon: all twenty plan prompts answered from the validated design file, no manual driving. Two absence-class defects the vision judge cannot see reliably - missing 'OT Refs:/NT Refs:' labels and face-forward figures - now have reference-free focused gates in the grade phase (same pattern as the placeholder-leak gate). Lesson recorded: a schema-invalid descriptor edit silently broke the live gate; pytest exit codes are now checked explicitly.

BATCH 4 (#047-#051): REDEEMER, BRICK, BABBLE, ENOCH, ABRAM. User rulings encoded: a look is only a kicker if the player can act on it (WATCHMAN reworked); the set's canvas is the whole antediluvian-to-Babel era, not the tower by default; each set is one fallen kingdom in order and Egypt is set 2 (EGYPT pulled from slot 050 before planning, ENOCH takes it). Root cause of NAME/COMMON style drift found: the curated finished-card reference manifest fed a pre-matrix MOSES example (caps rarity, hollow diamond, heavy borders, Nile scene) to every NAME/COMMON render - retired; SHINAR and ABRAM re-rendered on the template alone. Refs lines now ship with their labels baked in like verse lines; the descriptor pins title-case rarity text; the quantity grammar accepts 'another player' (first gift-to-a-rival design, held back for set 2).

ART STYLE RESTORED (user: 'we've lost the original art style I enjoyed with vibrant colors and impressionistic art'). Every art prompt I had written said 'engraved devotional style on warm parchment tones' - my invention. The authority is the printed set (example cards 001-020): luminous cinematic oil painting, deep shadowed fields lit by one radiant golden light, saturated blues and golds, symbolic subjects. Rule encoded in the descriptor (art_direction.style_rule), the metadata prompt, the recipe doc, and memory; all 20 art prompts rewritten; all 20 faces repainted panel-only via image-only revise (ELDER and GATHER needed fresh rebuilds after pip wobble), every one 100/100 and eyeballed. Stat rubric proposed (LORE/CONTEXT/COMPLEXITY definitions with anchors, 10/25/30/25/10 target shape, optional rarity sum caps) - awaiting the user's two calls before rescoring.

DETERMINISTIC FIXED ELEMENTS (user principle: 'setting things deterministically should most always be a deterministic method' - prove no quality loss). hypertext.cards.fixed_elements stamps stat pips (template ring glyphs), type pill (template block + CARD_TYPE word), rarity chip with cost glyphs (template, block recolored to the face's navy), collector number and series footer (Liberation Serif at template size) with per-region registration and provenance; proof on BRICK and REDEEMER: pip + cost gates green, judge 100/100 with 3-0 votes, 0.95% of pixels touched. Found in passing: all four TITLE composed templates carry a NOUN pill (staged in the Lot ledger's template matrix). Also: the /tmp scratch tooling was wiped between turns - loop scripts, driver daemon, and this tracker's generator now live in scripts/pipeline and scripts/babel with state in series/2026-Q1/tracker-state.json. Stat rubric encoded (LORE weight, CONTEXT frequency buckets, COMPLEXITY history); 20 cards rescored on record, pip rows to be re-stamped deterministically.

TEMPLATE DEFECT #2 - UNCOMMON chip (found via ledger comment on the BRICK proof: 'the rarity escaped the pill'). All five composed */uncommon templates set 'Uncommon' 12px from the chip block's left edge where the other rarities use ~32px, clipping the U; the image model had been quietly widening the chip on every UNCOMMON render, so the deterministic stamp was the first thing to expose it. Fix in fixed_elements: chip_geometry() measures block, word and diamond on the template; correct_chip_patch() extends the block left and re-sets the word in Liberation Serif at the template's cap height and colour whenever the word is clipped; stamp_chip() also covers any wider model-painted chip with the face's own parchment. Test asserts the word sits at the set inset for all 20 templates. BRICK re-stamped from the model render: gates green, judge 100/100 3-0, 1.2% pixels touched. Lesson: every element copied from a template needs a geometry assertion, not just a hash.

RARITY CHIP: VERIFIED, NOT STAMPED (user, on the BRICK proof: the stamped chip 'doesn't blend into the card like the original did'). Side by side with model-painted UNCOMMON chips (SEED, MESSENGER, BRICK's own render) the stamped chip was flat navy with a hard outline and a thinner word; the painted chips carry a soft gradient, doubled outline and a halo. Decision: the chip is the one fixed element where the model beats the template, so it stays Gemini output and hypertext.cards.rarity_chip_gate makes it deterministic the other way - block, word width, inset, gap, cap height and diamond colour measured against the canonical template, wired into hypertext visual-gate and the pipeline gate beside the pip and cost gates. Stamp scope is now pips, type pill, number, footer. BRICK re-stamped from the model render with its own chip: 0.94% of pixels touched, chip region byte-identical, gates green. Template defects (TITLE pill, UNCOMMON chip) are handled by scripts/templates/repair_composed_labels.py (user runs --apply).

STAMP WIRED INTO THE PIPELINE + 20 FACES RE-STAMPED. daily._run_stat_pip_visual_gate now applies the fixed-elements stamp (pips, type pill, number, footer) to every freshly rendered face before the pip, cost and chip gates; grade/review never stamp. The image prompt zeroes the three stat fields and tells the model to paint every pip empty - pips are set only by the stamp. All 20 rescored cards (#032-#051) re-stamped from their model renders, gates green, judge 100/100 with 3-0 style votes on every one. Batch found one stamp bug: the number cover took parchment from a fixed x that the wide ADJECTIVE pill reaches, pasting 'VE' over the number on HIGH/DEEP/DARK/FILLED (and silently on FOREIGN); the cover now sits relative to the measured pill box and the five were re-run clean.

TEMPLATE PACKAGE REPAIRED (user: 'just run the template repair'). scripts/templates/repair_composed_labels.py --apply rewrote eight golden PNGs: four TITLE pills now read TITLE, five UNCOMMON chips set 'Uncommon' inside the block, from two SHA-pinned Liberation Serif patches declared in composed/manifest.json; persistence manifest and verifier re-pinned, verifier extended to expect and digest-check the patches; package verification PASS; the two guarded package tests now run and pass. Compromise noted: the repair condenses 'Uncommon' 13% to fit the existing block while the model paints it full-width in a wider block; the rarity chip gate now expects word width from the COMMON word scaled by font metrics (-25%/+12%) so both conventions pass and all twenty current faces stay green. Commit 619da56.

BATCH 5 (#052-#056: HOVER, NEW, DESTROYER, SHEPHERD, ASCEND) - the first batch produced end to end under the full contract: designs validated offline against the seed/candidate validators and the stat rubric before any model call (the printed-rating estimator is a hard constraint: a COMMON carries no condition, no Letter gain, no second draw - so NEW and SHEPHERD left their grammar families), daemon-driven plan, render with the model painting empty pips, deterministic stamp inside the pipeline gate, pip/cost/chip gates, judge. Found in passing: the model paints its type pill and '#' a little wider than the template's, so the stamp now clears the model's dark pixels around the pill and widens the number cover (NEW #053 showed a pill sliver and a '#' ghost). WHY NEW TOOK SIX RENDERS, FIXED: (1) crowd art prompt -> face-forward figures twice; metadata prompt and descriptor figure_rule now forbid crowds/groups (prefer no people, else one figure from behind); (2) self-heal now repaints the art panel for a figure-rule failure at any score instead of re-rolling the whole card; (3) 42-word ability garbled twice -> per-rarity render word caps in the validator (COMMON 34, UNCOMMON 40, RARE 48, GLORIOUS 56) with prompt guidance, NEW shortened to 34 words and re-rendered; (4) self-heal archives every attempt's grade.txt under outputs/grades/. Also re-rendered ASCEND (pale first face, garbled 38-word copy fixed) and DEEP (its face was still the alternate deep-sea style; standard style is the default) - all three at 100/100 3-0.

BATCH 6 (#057-#061: DISCORD, DEPART, CHOSEN, EDEN, FIRE), timed. Design + offline validation 17:14:18-17:17:56 (3m38s); daemon-driven plan, render, stamp, gates, judge 17:17:56-17:23:58 (6m02s) - about 72s per card, six renders for five cards (DEPART's first roll leaked DEFINITION TEXT). All five 100/100 with 3-0 style votes; no self-heal fixes needed. The post-mortem fixes held: no crowds, every ability inside its word cap, first-render pass rate 4/5. Designs at scripts/pipeline/designs/batch6_057_061.py.

ONE LEMMA, ONE CARD (user: 'if we have a word in a different tense, like Choose, we should not have derivatives unless they use different lemma'). hypertext.cards.lemma_uniqueness rejects a candidate that shares a printed Hebrew or Greek lemma, a Hebrew root (consonant skeleton of the transliteration), or an English stem with any existing card; hard fail in the plan phase after metadata, plus 'hypertext lemma-audit --series'. Proper-name/noun homographs (SHEM / NAME) are exempt. CHOSEN #059 retired (bachar/bachir, eklegomai/eklektos vs CHOOSE #043) and the slot regenerated as FAITHFUL (neeman / pistos) in five minutes, 100/100 first render. The audit found three more collisions, all involving a legacy card or BABBLE: BABBLE #049 prints exactly CONFUSE #006's lemmas (balal / syncheo); BRICK #048 and STONE #008 both print lithos; WATCHMAN #046 and KEEPER #019 both print phylax. Awaiting the user's call on which card yields in each pair.

CREATIVITY RULES (user: 'We aren\'t being creative enough with abilities. I think hover does the same thing as kingdom… it could have utilized hovering over the pages'; 'a letter is worth three cards… we need creativity using the mechanics'). (1) Shape-uniqueness: hypertext.cards.ability_shape signs every ability (core gain verb+zone+quantity, reach, look count, bottom, filter, cost, condition, rest destination, put source, secondary gain, opponent effect, shuffle, delayed); identical shapes fail the plan phase; 'hypertext ability-audit --series --show'. HOVER v1 = KINGDOM confirmed by the check. (2) Letters weigh three cards: an unconditional Letter gain is payoff 3, a conditional one 2, forcing another player to spend a Letter is interaction 2. (3) Design palette now demands Letters, Lots, or Pages on at least two of five cards per batch, with concrete patterns; the estimator scores Page/Lot-driven scaling as setup 2 / payoff 3 and accepts a single 'Page' as the Pages zone. Redesigned and re-rendered at 100/100 3-0: HOVER v2 (one card of each card type in another player\'s Page, from Sheol), FIRE v2 (reveal the top card into Sheol; a VERB earns a Letter), DARK v2 (cover the top, take from the bottom; v1 shared WATCHMAN\'s shape). Remaining shape duplicates are all legacy #001-#031.

LEMMA AUDIT RESOLVED (user: 'keep brick and keeper'). STONE #008 -> petra (Matt 16:18; legacy face regenerates with the legacy pass), WATCHMAN #046 -> gregoreo (Mark 13:37), BABBLE #049 -> Bavel / battalogeo (Gen 11:9 / Matt 6:7).
